title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of the 'Longue Marche' study of the modular tower. Write S0^+ = SL(2,Z) and Π = Γ(2). Π0 is the index-2 subgroup of Γ(2) generated by λ_i = -ℓ_i. It contains no -1 and maps isomorphically onto Γ(2)/±1, i.e. onto π1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Π00 is the normal closure of δ = λ1λ0^{-1} = ℓ1ℓ0^{-1} = [[1,2],[2,5]]. It has index 3 in Π0 and contains [Π0,Π0]. The previous page guessed that Π00 is a congruence subgroup of level 12, normal of index 36 in SL(2,Z), with image of order 32 in SL(2,Z/12) (order 1152).

This page checks that guess.

(111) δ^2 = [[5,12],[12,29]] ≡ 5·I (mod 12). Since 25 ≡ 1, δ^4 ≡ 1 (mod 12).

(112) Several congruences follow:
- δ ≡ 1 (mod 2) but δ ≢ 1 (mod 4), while δ^2 ≡ 1 (mod 4).
- δ ≢ 1 (mod 3), and δ^2 ≡ -1 (mod 3).
- So the mod-3 image of δ has order 4 and lies in the quaternion 2-Sylow subgroup of SL(2,F3).

(113) Use SL(2,Z/12) ≅ SL(2,Z/4) × SL(2,Z/3) and the map u×v onto S0^+/Π0 × A3, of orders 12 × 3.
- u: SL(2,Z/4) → SL(2,Z)/Π0 is surjective because Π0 ⊃ Γ(4). Its kernel is the Klein four-group μ×μ.
- Concretely, in Ker(SL(2,Z/4) → SL(2,Z/2)) = {I+2X : X ∈ sl(2,F2)} ≅ F2^3, the images of the λ_i span a 2-dimensional complement to the scalars.
- The three non-trivial elements are the images of λ0, λ1, λ∞, permuted by ρ. Each has order 2 mod 4, so the product of two is the third; δ mod 4 equals λ∞ mod 4.
- v: SL(2,F3) → PSL(2,F3) ≅ A4 (acting on the 4 points of P^1(F3)) → A4/V4 ≅ Z/3. Its kernel is the 2-Sylow subgroup, of order 8.

Ker(u×v) has order 4·8 = 32 and index 36, and it contains δ mod 12. Combined with the a priori information from the previous page (image order a multiple of 32), the normal closure of δ mod 12 is exactly this kernel, of order 32.

This can also be checked directly by Goursat-type conjugation arguments: the normal closure contains V4 × 1 and 1 × Q8.

Conclusion, summarised on the next page: Π00 is the preimage of V4 × Q8. It is a normal congruence subgroup of level 12 and index 36. Geometrically (not said on this page), Π0/Π00 ≅ Z/3 with all λ_i mapping to the same generator. This is the cyclic triple cover y^3 = x(x-1) of the λ-line, totally ramified at 0, 1, ∞: the genus-1 curve with j = 0.
errors: No error on this page; all matrix computations check out: δ^2 = [[5,12],[12,29]], δ^4 ≡ 1 mod 12, δ^2 ≡ -1 mod 3.

The phrase 'dont l'ordre a priori était multiple de 32' depends on the unproved presumption from the previous page that Π00 contains Γ(12). The normal-closure equality can be verified directly, so the gap is harmless.

On the next page the 2-Sylow subgroup of SL(2,F3) is written '≃ D_4 [?]'. It is the quaternion group Q8, not dihedral; this is either a slip or a transcription error. The fact δ^2 ≡ -1 (mod 3) on this page already shows the element of order 4 squares to the central -1, as in Q8.

ideas.what: Π0, the index-2 free complement of ±1 in Γ(2) generated by -ℓ_i, contains Γ(4). Its image in SL(2,Z/4) is a Klein four-group complementary to the scalars in sl(2,F2).
ideas.modern_name: level-4 congruence lift of π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) into SL(2,Z)
ideas.where_published: related material in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller/modular tower discussion); details unsure

ideas.what: The normal closure of λ1λ0^{-1} (index 3 in Π0) is a congruence subgroup of level 12. Its image in SL(2,Z/12) is V4 × Q8, of index 36.
ideas.modern_name: normal congruence subgroup of level 12 / genus-1 normal subgroup (j=0 cyclic cover)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; tabulated in Cummins–Pauli congruence subgroup tables

ideas.what: The decomposition SL(2,Z/12) ≅ SL(2,Z/4) × SL(2,Z/3), with SL(2,F3) → A4 → Z/3 having Q8 as kernel.
ideas.modern_name: CRT decomposition; binary tetrahedral group structure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification by explicit matrix and finite-group computation that a specific index-3 subgroup of the free part of Γ(2) is a level-12 congruence subgroup. The result is standard (it is the j=0 cyclic triple cover of the Legendre line) and is a known entry in congruence-subgroup tables.
transcription_corrections: Line on the λ_i: should read 'λ1λ0^{-1} = λ̇1λ̇0 = λ̇∞', with dots denoting images mod 4. The machine transcription lost the dots on λ0 and λ∞.
'v : Sl(2,Z/3Z) → S3' should be '→ S3^+' (the alternating group A3), consistent with (113).
'G_4 ⊂ S_{P^1(Z/3Z)}' is most likely 𝔄_4, the alternating group on the 4 points of P^1(F3), i.e. PSL(2,F3).

Final sentence reads roughly: 'Cela montre que c'est bien le sous-groupe distingué engendré par δ (dont l'ordre a priori était multiple de 32), et ...'. The word 'engendré' was replaced by 'distingué' in an insertion.
